title: Consolidated smoke and perf eval harness for upgrade rollouts and LTS gating
creator: Riley Mathews
description: Create a single, reusable validation harness that runs fast smoke tests, targeted perf regression gates, and core eval suites before automated upgrades or LTS promotion. The harness must work for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and integrate with the rollout controller to allow automated hold/rollback decisions based on objective gates.
acceptance_criteria: Smoke test battery that completes within 90s for a standard canary (10 requests across chat/generate/embeddings)
Perf regression gate that compares tail latency P95 and p99 against a stable baseline and fails when regression >10%
Eval suite runner that can execute existing prompt-based evals and report quality deltas per model and prompt set
Integration with rollout controller: pass/fail signals emitted to canary automation and documented in console rollout timeline
Harness supports LTS promotion workflow: optional stricter gates and a hold window for manual review
Automated rollback trigger documented and tested in a dry-run
testing_matrix: Hosted API canary (us-east-1) - small model, 5 concurrent users
Dedicated pool staging - reserved capacity with burst disabled
Private (VPC) - air-gapped smoke via bastion and synthetic workload
LTS promotion workflow - stricter perf thresholds and eval pass rate threshold
rollout_plan: Phase 1: implement harness and a minimal smoke + perf gate for runtime-1.24 canaries. Phase 2: wire harness into rollout controller and add LTS-specific stricter gates. Phase 3: run two full LTS promotion rehearsals with on-call and SRE sign-offs.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Riley Mathews: Initial ticket created after postmortem for ENG-10211 upgrade flakiness. Proposed a unified harness to reduce disparate ad-hoc checks.

2026-02-20 - Asha Patel: Spike completed; prototype smoke runner implemented in infra-ci repo (see PR below). Found that KV cache warmup dominates early latency — added a cache-warmup step to smoke tests.
2026-02-27 - Ben Cho (SRE): Suggested adding a short synthetic tail-latency test at steady-state to detect kernel regression that only appears after 30s of sustained traffic.

2026-03-03 - PM review (Lina Gomez): Confirmed LTS gate needs a higher bar for embedding regressions because customers rely on stable embeddings for similarity search. Added embedding-specific evals to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-08 - Asha Patel: Implemented perf comparator and baseline snapshot storage in S3. Running nightly against canary baseline. Observed one perf regression in runtime-1.24-alpha; triggered a hold in the rehearsed rollout and created ENG-10902 to address.
2026-03-10 - Design review (Marta Ivanov): Requested small UX surface in Console rollout timeline to surface which gate failed and link to failing eval artifacts. Filed DES-214 for Console change.
2026-03-10 - Asha Patel: Marking progress; core harness merged behind feature flag. Next: add LTS stricter thresholds and run a full rehearsal with SRE and PM present.
notes: Trade-offs: stricter gates reduce blast radius but increase release latency. We will iterate thresholds based on one rehearsal and rollback noise metrics.
We opted to keep smoke tests lightweight (<=90s) so automated canaries can execute quickly and not block fast patch releases.
Baseline storage: monthly snapshot retention for perf baselines; older baselines archived to reduce S3 costs.
Owner for LTS signoff will be rotation between Release Engineering and SRE teams.
Plan to expose gate outcomes in Console with a link to raw eval artifacts and a diff summary to help PMs and engineers triage quickly.
